Changelog

Source: NEWS.md

LCZ4r 0.2.0

Breaking changes

  • lcz_get_parameters(iselect = ...) now really returns only the selected layers. Previously iselect was silently ignored while istack = TRUE (the default), so code that relied on receiving the full stack must drop iselect or set istack = TRUE explicitly.
  • lcz_get_parameters(istack = FALSE) now returns a named list of rasters, as documented, instead of throwing an error.
  • lcz_get_parameters(ishp = TRUE) dissolves polygons by class (one row per LCZ class) instead of returning every contiguous patch.
  • lcz_cal_area() returns lcz, lcz.name, lcz.col, count, area_km2 and area_perc; Area_Km2 is gone.
  • raster is no longer a dependency; all raster operations use terra.
  • tidyr moved from Suggests to Imports (it was already used at runtime).
  • Default plot titles are now empty and captions default to a translated “Source: LCZ4r” (previously hardcoded English strings).

New features

  • lang argument in every exported function ("en" by default). 11 languages: English, Portuguese, Spanish, French, Chinese (Simplified), German, Italian, Japanese, Korean, Russian and Arabic.
  • lcz_langs(), lcz_set_lang() and lcz_tr() for programmatic access.
  • Localised LCZ class names, axis labels, legends, plot titles and console messages.
  • Language aliases (pt-BR, zh-Hans, es-419, …) and graceful fallback to English for unsupported codes.
  • lcz_plot_map(max_pixels = ) to keep national/continental maps fast and memory-bounded.
  • lcz_fit_variogram(): three-level fallback for unstable variogram fits.
  • Unified visual grammar: lcz_theme_journal(), lcz_theme_map(), lcz_theme_series(), lcz_palette() and translated class names shared by every plot.
  • lcz_save_figure(): journal-sized export (120/190 mm, 600 dpi, PDF/SVG).
  • dev/ workflow, agent briefs, dev/check-i18n.R and dev/benchmark.R.
  • testthat suite covering i18n, parameters, areas, plots, time series, diagnostics and the figure system.

Terminology review (LCZ class names)

All 17 class names were reviewed against published national nomenclatures. Highlights:

  • Class G is a land-cover type, so “Water” is translated as water bodies (pt: “Corpos d’água”, es: “Cuerpos de agua”, fr: “Surface en eau”, de: “Gewässer”, it: “Corpi idrici”, zh: 水体, ja: 水域, ko: 수역, ru: Водоёмы, ar: مسطحات مائية).
  • French now follows the Cerema national LCZ nomenclature (Ensemble compact de tours, Bâtiments bas de grande emprise, …).
  • German follows the LCZ nomenclature used in German urban-climate reports (Kompakte hohe Bebauung, Gewässer, …).
  • Spanish follows the Argentine peer-reviewed nomenclature (SciELO/AJEA).
  • Russian follows the published LCZ table (Vestnik SGUGIT; Obukhov 2024).
  • Chinese/Japanese/Korean follow, respectively, the GEE Chinese LCZ catalogue, Mochida et al. and KEI/KPA usage.
  • Portuguese: “Esparsamente construída” → “Ocupação esparsa”; “Leve de baixa altura” → “Construções leves de baixa altura”; “Grande de baixa altura” → “Grandes construções de baixa altura”.

The full 17 × 11 table with sources is in dev/terminology.md.

Figure design (Nature/Science-level)

  • New lcz_theme_journal() and lcz_save_figure(): 120/190 mm column widths, 600 dpi or vector output, sans-serif 11 pt type scale, left-aligned titles and no top/right spines.
  • lcz_save_figure() writes PDF (cairo, fonts embedded), SVG (svglite) or PNG/TIFF (ragg), falling back gracefully when optional packages are absent.
  • Colour-blind-safe Okabe-Ito palette is now the default for categorical series (palette = "okabe"); sequential variables use viridis/magma and anomalies a symmetric blue-white-red scale.
  • lcz_uhi_intensity(group = TRUE) no longer uses a dual y-axis: it now draws two aligned panels, (a) urban/rural temperature and (b) UHI intensity.
  • lcz_anomaly() uses a symmetric diverging scale, ordered bars and a corrected dot plot (horizontal axis = air temperature, colour = anomaly).
  • lcz_ts() uses 0.55 pt lines, adaptive date labels, “LCZ n” facet labels and warming stripes centred on the series mean.
  • lcz_plot_map() gains optional scalebar/north_arrow, drawn in data coordinates without extra dependencies, and a single-column legend by default (legend_ncol = 2 available) so the map keeps its area.
  • lcz_plot_parameters() and lcz_plot_interp() use horizontal 70-75 mm colour bars, units in the scale title and a translated legend title.
  • Figure heights adapt to content: anomalies grow with the number of stations and area charts with the number of classes.
  • Full specification and checklist: dev/design-system.md.

Bug fixes

  • Removed options(warn = -1) from the map getters; it permanently silenced all warnings in the user’s session.
  • Fixed the unreachable z0 = 1 branch for LCZ class 2.
  • Fixed ldw typo in lcz_uhi_intensity() (line width was ignored).
  • Fixed urban/rural station matching by name, which collapsed groups when a station name appeared at several coordinates; selection now uses location.
  • Fixed vector recycling when Turban/Trural contain several stations.
  • Fixed lcz_ts() producing an empty plot when no station could be assigned to an LCZ class.
  • Fixed gstat.cv(nfold = 5) failing on time steps with fewer than five observations.
  • Fixed lcz_plot_map() mixing raster and terra and copying whole rasters.
  • Fixed lcz_plot_interp() copying whole rasters just to compute min/max.
  • Replaced deprecated tibble::as.tibble().
  • Corrected the TRC unit in lcz_plot_parameters() ([-], not [m]).
  • Area labels in lcz_cal_area() now match the km² axis (were percentages).

Diagnostics and robustness

  • lcz_uhi_intensity() no longer emits openair’s “duplicate dates” warning: stations are averaged within each reference group before the time aggregation, so timeAverage() sees one row per group per timestamp.

  • lcz_check_raster() now selects the layer named lcz (or class) in multi-layer stacks instead of blindly taking layer 2. This fixes failures when a stack’s first layer is the LCZ map.

  • lcz_uhi_intensity() now reports how many stations matched the map and which LCZ classes were found before failing, instead of a generic “no urban/rural stations” message.

  • When no station falls inside the map, the error now explicitly points to the raster extent/CRS and the station coordinates.

Performance

Measured on a 300 × 300 raster (90k cells), R 4.5.1:

Function Before After Speed-up
lcz_get_parameters(istack = TRUE) 8.35 s 0.10 s ~83×
lcz_ts(extract.method = "two.step") 2.65 s 0.16 s ~16×
lcz_plot_map() 0.25 s 0.07 s ~3.6×
lcz_cal_area(iplot = FALSE) 0.10 s 0.03 s ~3.3×

Documentation

  • New package-level help page: ?LCZ4r lists the general and local functions, languages and the figure system.
  • README (English, Portuguese, Spanish and Chinese) now documents the 11 languages, the journal figure system and quick-start examples for maps and UHI figures.
  • dev/design-system.md: figure specification and review checklist.
  • dev/terminology.md: 17 LCZ classes x 11 languages with sources.
  • AUDITORIA.md: technical and scientific audit of the 0.2.0 changes.

Internal

  • Translation engine in R/aaa-i18n-core.R, one file per language.
  • Shared helpers in R/lcz_utils.R and R/lcz_map_helpers.R.
  • The three map getters now delegate to a single clip/download pipeline.

Known limitations

  • lcz_anomaly_map() and lcz_interp_eval() can still fail on very small station networks (< 5 stations per LCZ class); this predates 0.2.0.
  • The SAD (surface admittance) rows of the LCZ parameter table mix units and need to be verified against Stewart & Oke (2012), Table 3.
  • Vignettes live in vignettes-<lang>/ and are not built by R CMD build.

Translation status

The de, it, ja, ko, ru and ar catalogues were written for this release and should be reviewed by native speakers before a CRAN submission.
